sections.text:
1 Expeditionem imperatoris Conradi III, a. 1147 p. C., pro calamitate rei publi-
cae habuerunt Byzantini, vide e. g. Nicet. Chron., I, 4, p. 80, 9 : νέφος πολεμίων
ἐκ τῶν ἑσπερίων ἐπισυστὰν κλιμάτων, τετριγὸς δεινὸν καὶ ὀλέθριον, ἐς τὰ
Ῥωμαίων ἐνέσκηψεν ὅρια, ἡ τῶν Ἀλαμανῶν, φημί, κίνησις .. Illam calamitatem
apparitione cometae significatam fuisse alibi non inveni.
2 De prodigiis qui adventum Occidentalium regnante Alexio portenderunt, cf.
Muralt, Chronologie byzantine, ad annum 1095, p. 73, n° 3.
sections.en:
1 The Byzantines considered the expedition of the emperor Conrad III, in the year 1147 A.D., as a calamity for the state, see e.g. Nicetas Choniates, Chronicon, I, 4, p. 80, 9: "a cloud of enemies having gathered from the western climes, creaking terribly and destructively, fell upon the borders of the Romans, I mean the movement of the Alamanni.." I have not found elsewhere that that calamity was signified by the appearance of a comet.
2 Concerning the prodigies which portended the arrival of the Westerners during the reign of Alexios, cf. Muralt, Chronologie byzantine, ad annum 1095, p. 73, n° 3.

summary.headline: Comets as Omens and Signs
summary.text: Interpretation of the Bethlehem star as either an angel or comet, with comets described as omens of great worldly changes. Examples include the comet preceding the Alamanni’s passage through Romania under Conrad III and Alexios, and the miraculous eclipse recognized by Dionysius the Areopagite after hearing Paul preach Christ.
